    Stomach and gut contents of juvenile common sole

    soles_stomach.Rd

    Diet composition and digestive tract contents of juvenile common sole (Solea solea) sampled during the CAPES project.

    Format

    A tibble with 29 variables:

    sample_TAG

    Character. Identifier of the sampled fish.

    class

    Character. Fish age class, including "G0", "G1", and "G2".

    zone

    Character. Sampling area within the Seine estuary.

    site

    Character. Sampling-site identifier.

    date

    Sampling date.

    hour

    Sampling time.

    sex

    Character. Sex of the sampled fish.

    mass_stomach_full_g

    Numeric. Mass of the stomach including its contents, expressed in grams.

    mass_stomach_empty_g

    Numeric. Mass of the empty stomach, expressed in grams.

    mass_stomach_content_g

    Numeric. Mass of the stomach contents, expressed in grams.

    mass_gut_full_g

    Numeric. Mass of the gut including its contents, expressed in grams.

    mass_gut_empty_g

    Numeric. Mass of the empty gut, expressed in grams.

    mass_gut_content_g

    Numeric. Mass of the gut contents, expressed in grams.

    observations_tutorial

    Character. Additional observations recorded during the examination of the digestive tract.

    species

    Character. Taxonomic identification of the prey item or other biological material recorded in the digestive tract. Identification may be provided at different taxonomic levels.

    status

    Character. Status assigned to the identified item, used to distinguish prey from other recorded material.

    N_stomach

    Numeric. Number of prey individuals or items recorded in the stomach.

    degradation_stage_stomach

    Degradation stage of the prey material found in the stomach.

    N_gut

    Numeric. Number of prey individuals or items recorded in the gut.

    degradation_stage_gut

    Degradation stage of the prey material found in the gut.

    N_tract

    Numeric. Total number of prey individuals or items recorded in the digestive tract.

    observations

    Character. Additional observations concerning the identified item, including morphological characteristics, body fragments, and information used for taxonomic identification or prey counting.

    length_TL_cm

    Numeric. Total fish length, expressed in centimetres.

    length_SL_cm

    Numeric. Standard fish length, expressed in centimetres.

    mass_tot_gww

    Numeric. Total fish wet mass, expressed in grams wet weight (g ww).

    mass_liver_mgww

    Numeric. Liver wet mass, expressed in milligrams wet weight (mg ww).

    mass_tractus_mgww

    Numeric. Digestive tract wet mass, expressed in milligrams wet weight (mg ww).

    mass_gonads_gww

    Numeric. Gonad wet mass, expressed in grams wet weight (g ww).

    mass_eviceratedd_mgww

    Numeric. Eviscerated fish wet mass, expressed in milligrams wet weight (mg ww).

    Source

    CAPES project, Seine estuary. Juvenile common sole stomach and gut content dataset.

    Details

    The dataset contains fish identification and biological characteristics, digestive tract measurements, and taxonomic information on prey items identified in the stomach and gut. Prey abundance, degradation stage, and identification notes are recorded separately for the two digestive compartments.

    Each fish can be represented by several rows corresponding to different prey taxa or other items identified in its digestive tract. Fish-level information, including morphometric measurements and digestive tract masses, may therefore be repeated across rows sharing the same sample_TAG.

    Prey abundance is recorded separately for the stomach (N_stomach) and gut (N_gut), as well as for the complete digestive tract (N_tract).

    The species variable contains the taxonomic identification recorded during the analysis. Some items are identified only to genus or a higher taxonomic level, whereas others remain unidentified.

    The status variable can be used to select prey observations before analysing diet composition.

    Missing values indicate that the corresponding measurement or information was not available for the observation.
